# Community code of conduct

ChemRxn welcomes contributors across chemistry, scientific documents, agents, tools, evaluation, and
product design. We want technically rigorous disagreement without personal hostility or unsafe disclosure.

## Expected behavior

- Be respectful, specific, and patient with contributors of different disciplines and experience levels.
- Critique evidence, code, contracts, and scientific reasoning rather than people.
- Distinguish source observation from inference, uncertainty from error, and preliminary results from locked
  claims.
- Give credit for code, data, designs, experiments, and prior work; preserve required attribution.
- Protect credentials, personal information, private papers/data, benchmark GT, and security-sensitive details.
- Disclose material AI/Agent assistance and take human responsibility for the submitted work.
- Accept maintainer requests to narrow a change, add evidence/tests, move it to the correct extension layer,
  or pause it for scientific/security/licensing review.

## Unacceptable behavior

- harassment, discrimination, threats, sexualized conduct, insults, or sustained personal attacks;
- publishing another person's private information, credentials, source material, or security report;
- fabricating evidence, results, provenance, authorship, tests, or chemical validation;
- knowingly bypassing anti-leakage, frozen-scorer, immutable-artifact, or source-rights boundaries;
- automated Issue/PR spam or submitting Agent-generated work the contributor cannot explain;
- retaliation against good-faith scientific, security, accessibility, or licensing review.

## Scope and enforcement

This applies in repository Issues, PRs, reviews, discussions, shared development environments, and project
communications. Maintainers may edit, hide, close, reject, or revert contributions and may temporarily or
permanently restrict participation when needed to protect the community or project.

Report conduct concerns privately to the repository owner through an existing private channel. Do not post
sensitive conduct reports publicly. Include relevant links, dates, context, and desired safety constraints;
remove unrelated credentials and private scientific data.

Maintainers will handle reports as privately and impartially as practical, while recognizing that immediate
safety, legal, employment, or platform obligations may require escalation.
